'''Seppo Ilmari Linnainmaa''' (born 28 September 1945) is a [[Finns|Finnish]] [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]] known for creating the modern version of [[backpropagation]].

== Biography ==
He was born in [[Pori]].<ref>{{cite book | editor=Ellonen, Leena | title=Suomen professorit 1640–2007 | page=405 | location=Helsinki | publisher=Professoriliitto | year=2008 | isbn=978-952-99281-1-8 | language=Finnish }}</ref> He received his MSc in 1970 and introduced a reverse mode of [[automatic differentiation]] in his MSc thesis.<ref name="lin1970"></ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Seppo Linnainmaa (Mathematician and Computer Scientist) |url=https://www.onthisday.com/people/seppo-linnainmaa |access-date=2024-04-06 |website=OnThisDay.com |language=en}}</ref> In 1974 he obtained the first doctorate ever awarded in computer science at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref name="grie2012" /> In 1976, he became Assistant Professor. From 1984 to 1985 he was Visiting Professor at the [[University of Maryland]], USA. From 1986 to 1989 he was Chairman of the Finnish Artificial Intelligence Society. From 1989 to 2007, he was Research Professor at the [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland|VTT Technical Research Centre]] of [[Finland]]. He retired in 2007.

== Backpropagation ==
Explicit, efficient error [[backpropagation]] in arbitrary, discrete, possibly sparsely connected, [[neural networks]]-like networks was first described in Linnainmaa's 1970 master's thesis,<ref name="lin1970" /><ref name="lin1976" /> albeit without reference to NNs,<ref name="Schmidhuber2015">Jürgen Schmidhuber, (2015). [http://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/who-invented-backpropagation.html Who Invented Backpropagation?]</ref> when he introduced the reverse mode of [[automatic differentiation]] (AD), in order to efficiently compute the [[derivative]] of a [[Differentiable function|differentiable]] [[composite function]] that can be represented as a [[graph of a function|graph]], by recursively applying the [[chain rule]] to the building blocks of the function.<ref name="grie2012">{{cite book |last1=Griewank |first1=Andreas |year=2012 |chapter=Who Invented the Reverse Mode of Differentiation? |title=Documenta Mathematica, Extra Volume ISMP |pages=389–400 |s2cid=15568746 |chapter-url=https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/documenta/vol-ismp/52_griewank-andreas-b.pdf |archive-date=2023-12-15 |access-date=2022-03-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215034634/https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/documenta/vol-ismp/52_griewank-andreas-b.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="lin1970">{{cite thesis |authorlink1=Seppo Linnainmaa |first1=Seppo |last1=Linnainmaa |year=1970 |title=Algoritmin kumulatiivinen pyöristysvirhe yksittäisten pyöristysvirheiden Taylor-kehitelmänä |trans-title=The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors |language=Finnish |pages=6–7 |url=https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/linnainmaa1970thesis.pdf }}</ref><ref name="lin1976">{{cite journal |first=Seppo |last=Linnainmaa |authorlink=Seppo Linnainmaa |year=1976 |title=Taylor expansion of the accumulated rounding error |journal=BIT Numerical Mathematics |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=146–160 |doi=10.1007/BF01931367 |s2cid=122357351 }}</ref> Linnainmaa published it first, following Gerardi Ostrowski who had used it in the context of certain process models in chemical engineering some five years earlier, but didn't publish.
